literal: instrument; device that holds or restrains

definitions.definition: A diagram (drawn, engraved or built) in which a deity and its mantra are installed and worshipped; used across the Śākta, Śaiva, Vaiṣṇava and Jain tantric traditions beside or instead of the maṇḍala.
The Śrīcakra: the Goddess's own form as nine interlocking triangles and enclosures.
Engraved diagrams such as the Siddhacakra and the Ṛṣimaṇḍala worshipped in Jain temples and homes.

cross_language.note: the Tibetan word renders yantra as 'machine' and names physical yoga exercises (trulkhor), not a worship diagram

definitions.definition: A follower of the tantras, as distinguished from the vaidika who follows the Veda alone; also the tantric ritual specialist.
In Kṣemarāja's scheme the Tāntrikas hold the self to be transcendent, the Kaulas immanent, the Trika both.
The 'very empty', second of the four empties of the completion stage.
The 'very void' reached when the knot of Viṣṇu is pierced in the second stage.
The 'great empty', third of the four empties.
The 'great void', abode of all powers, reached by the breath in the third stage.
The fourfold scheme of the Yoga śāstra modelled on medicine — saṃsāra, its cause, liberation, the means (YBh 2.15).
The four emanations (vyūha) of the Lord: Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha.

notes: Homonym: the same word names a fourfold expository scheme (Yoga, after medicine) and the Pāñcarātra doctrine of four emanations. Recorded so the two are not confused.

definitions.definition: The 'Imperturbable' buddha of the east and of the vajra family; he crowns the head of Ekajaṭā and Mahācīna-Tārā.
In the Hindu Tārā cult, Akṣobhya (sometimes a serpent) sits on Tārā's head; the Tārā texts name him as her consort.
Across the families, a revealed scripture of the mantra path (or, for the Buddhists, also the continuum of ground, path and fruit); the Jains speak rather of kalpas (mantra manuals).
The Pāñcarātra calls its revelations saṃhitās or tantras (the Lakṣmī Tantra), spoken by Nārāyaṇa.
The Śaiva six-limbed yoga, which includes reasoning (tarka) as a limb (Mṛgendra's yoga section; Mālinīvijayottara).
Six limbs — posture, breath-control, withdrawal, concentration, meditation, absorption — in the Gorakṣaśataka and Vivekamārtaṇḍa.
Used in the Māṇḍūkya-kārikā (4.90) for the teaching from which what is to be abandoned, known, attained and matured is learned; Śaṅkara glosses it as the foremost means.

notes: U49 contribution: records the Advaita use of a Mahāyāna self-designation (brw:mahayana-vocabulary-in-alatasanti).

definitions.definition: Epithet in GK 4.99 of the awakened one whose knowledge does not go out to objects; Śaṅkara explains it as 'pervasive like space' or 'protector'.
The chosen deity of an initiate, whose mantra he receives and with whom he identifies in worship.

cross_language.note: the meditational deity bound to the practitioner by pledge

definitions.definition: In Jain ritual manuals, the consecration and protection of the worshipper's body by placing the syllables of the homage to the five supreme beings on the limbs before worship.

notes: U49 contribution; recalled, to be checked.
